title: KoreLumina — Master OS - KoreLumina Reconstruction Update — message 4

metadata.content:
This is a good point to stop and assess before proceeding.
Those six modified files all belong to the same architectural change:


appearance/resolver/types.ts


appearance/resolver/resolveAppearance.ts


appearance/css/variables.ts


appearance/css/applyAppearance.ts


background/LuminaGlassLayer.tsx


surface/LuminaSurface.tsx


They represent one cohesive feature: promoting material rendering (saturation, contrast, brightness, layer opacity) to first-class appearance tokens.
The builds have passed repeatedly, so the changes are at least type-safe and build-clean. However, they have not yet been functionally validated. Based on the audit, there are still open questions:


Are the new CSS variables actually consumed everywhere?


Does LuminaSurface now use the new material tokens consistently?


Does switching between Glass, Solid, and Mica produce the intended visual differences?


Do Preview, Designer, and Developer workspaces all render identically?


I would not commit yet.
Instead, treat this as a pending feature branch. The next step should be functional validation:


Launch the builder.


Open Workspace Appearance.


Exercise every appearance control:


Material (Glass/Solid/Mica)


Tint


Transparency


Blur


Elevation


Glow


Contrast




Verify the visual changes propagate immediately.


Compare Designer, Developer, AI, and Preview workspaces for consistency.


If those checks pass, then commit this as a single logical change, for example:
Bashgit add \
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/appearance/css/applyAppearance.ts \
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/appearance/css/variables.ts \
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/appearance/resolver/resolveAppearance.ts \
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/appearance/resolver/types.ts \
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/background/LuminaGlassLayer.tsx \
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/surface/LuminaSurface.tsx

git commit -m "feat(appearance): promote material rendering to resolved appearance tokens"
After that commit, continue the broader workspace appearance audit from a clean working tree. That keeps the history aligned with your reconstruction workflow: one architectural feature per commit, followed by the next audit-driven improvement.
